notes.title: Bug fix and some minor corrections
notes.content:
The next update will be released a little later today and will include:

1. In the controls menu, a typo has been fixed so that when assigning the right mouse button to an action, it will now show as RMB instead of LMB.

2. If a savegame was made and then loaded while in the second part of Etyrial, the loot objects in the first part would become bugged and lose all their content. This has been fixed.

3. The range shown from the player to an enemy in the info panel had a slight deviation from the distance measured by the system when making an attack. This meant that players could be out of attack range even though it looked like they were close enough based on the info panel. This has now been corrected.

4. The Smithy quest in Olhenvey Town had an issue where the final part of the quest would, in rare cases, not trigger—resulting in the NPC not showing up, and the quest couldn't be completed. This has also been fixed.

notes.title: Minor corrections
notes.content:
The next update is almost ready:

1. In the prison camp in Etyrial, one of the stairs was blocked by an invisible wall; this has now been corrected.

2. An HP cap of 2300 on the Regeneration spell has been added.

notes.title: Bug fix and some corrections
notes.content:
The next update will be ready in a couple of hours:

1. The achievement for collecting all the Ruga fruits did not trigger. This is now corrected.

2. The achievement for killing the Storm Witch triggered just by killing one of her clones. This is now corrected.

3. A bug that caused merchant item prices to decrease on loading has now been corrected.

4. The Angle Shot skill has been fixed so that it now fires undodgeable arrows as it is supposed to.

5. Inconsistencies between the icon and information text for the Power Draw skill have been fixed.

6. A few typos and spelling inconsistencies have been corrected.

notes.title: Added achievements and some minor corrections
notes.content:
In a couple of hours, the next update will be ready.

1. 26 achievements have now been added to the game. Achievements will not be added retrospectively, so only goals completed after this update will unlock the corresponding achievement.

2. A test function had been left active by mistake in the previous build, which caused the shield skill to increase to level 4 if a specific key was pressed. This has now been disabled.

3. In the wave battle in the Dwarf King's Hall, if you killed all enemies in a single round before all waves were completed, the sequence would soft lock, making it impossible to progress without loading and redoing the battle. This has now been corrected.

notes.title: Quality update
notes.content:
Update coming later today:

1. I noticed that some quality settings were not set correctly, resulting in an unintended decrease in quality on some systems. This issue is particularly noticeable in the environment ground textures, which become blurry at a very short distance. This is a method for the game to reduce performance load, but it shouldn't happen at a distance where it's noticeable. This update fixes this issue and also raises a few other quality settings.

notes.title: Minor correction
notes.content: 1. Corrected a bug that meant players could discard shopkeepers' items.

notes.title: Minor corrections
notes.content:
1. Corrected a bug where saving while having the shop window open would override the player's inventory with the shop's items.

2. If the inventory window was open when entering a shop, the player could not move after closing the shop unless the inventory window was opened again and closed. This has also been corrected.

notes.title: Added a new spell and some minor corrections.
notes.content:
Later today, a new update will be released with the following changes:

1. Corrected a fault in the Viper Den in Rasunda, where some ambush enemies were visible.

2. Added a new spell, "Guiding Light," which creates a light source that follows the party around. This addition aims to reduce the need for adjusting the brightness on some monitors in dark areas. It's a first-level spell in the category of 'Healing Magic' and can be obtained in the same ways as other spells

3. Increased the item drop chance on rats and goblins.

4. Slightly increased the gold drop from rats and goblins.

notes.title: New difficulty setting and some corrections
notes.content:
In about two hours, the next update should be ready:

1. The shield skill previously ignored the defense power bonus it provides at levels 3 and 4, and the informational text was incorrect. This has now been rectified.

2. Some players have expressed a desire for an easier game, while others have requested more challenging gameplay. This illustrates the challenge of finding a difficulty level that satisfies all players. To address this, “Easy Mode” has been replaced with a difficulty dropdown menu. Players can now select from “Normal,” “Easy,” and “Hard” options. The new “Easy” setting further reduces difficulty compared to the old “Easy Mode.” Note that this change will reset the game's difficulty to normal. If you are currently playing on “Easy Mode” and wish to continue at this level, you will need to go to the menu and select the new easy difficulty.

notes.title: Ranger update
notes.content:
In a couple of hours, I will make an update that adds some changes to the Ranger class:

1. The skill attacks that use normal arrows, like Heavy Arrow and Double Shot, are now undodgeable.

2. The skill tree option for 'Enhanced Dexterity' now gives 2 extra damage per 3 points of dexterity instead of 1.

3. When the Ranger reaches level 15, the class is granted a new passive skill named 'Mystical Arrows'. This adds different random effects to all the Ranger's ranged attacks. These include 'Cripple', 'Burning', 'Powerless', 'Weakness', 'Acid Burn', and 'Sticky'.

notes.title: Scale UI To Resolution, and some corrections
notes.content:
The next update will be ready shortly:

1. The item compare panel has been locked to the item info panel, so they always show up next to each other.

2. Screen match size now saves and loads correctly.

3. A new option called "Scale UI To Resolution" has been added to the screen resolutions menu. By default, the UI elements are set to scale in such a way that they more or less occupy the same space on the screen regardless of the screen's resolution. Then the match size can be adjusted to decrease the size a bit if needed. This is to prevent UI objects from becoming so small that text, for instance, becomes unreadable. However, this does mean that UI elements can seem unnecessarily big on high resolutions. Enabling "Scale UI To Resolution" will scale the UI to the active resolution, which in most cases will result in considerably smaller UI.

notes.title: New function and some corrections
notes.content:
1. The Shaman skill "My Blood Is Your Life" was only working when the shaman received physical damage. This has been corrected so the skill also works when receiving all other damage types.

2. The auto-walk function has been deactivated in combat.

3. Some enemies that were wrongly placed in Etyrial have been removed. These enemies had no effect on the gameplay, but you could never encounter them. So, after the new function that tells if all enemies are defeated in an area was implemented, they blocked the function from triggering in Etyrial, since there were always these two enemies left on the map.

4. When moving the inventory window or the character outfit window, the new position will now be saved. So their position won't reset back to default when loading a game. This will also be expanded to the character stat window in a later update.

5. A very small number of players have experienced crashes in the Bastion boss fight in Etyrial, and only in this location. For these players, lowering the graphics has resolved the issues. Therefore, I have made a small change to a shader in that location, as it's the only thing related to graphics that I can find that differs from all other locations in the game. It's a long shot but worth a try.

notes.title: Area cleared notifications, separate music/ambience volume control, and more
notes.content:
The next update is ready and will be available shortly. Here are the changes:

1. Added the ability to change the volume of out-of-combat world ambiance and in-combat music separately.

2. Added a function that prints a message in the information window when all enemies in the area have been defeated and looted. It also triggers when entering an area.

3. Added a function that prints a message in the information window when all loot objects, like chests in the area, have been looted. It also triggers when entering an area.

4. Made some corrections to prevent red slime in Dralavia from being able to spawning inside a cliff. There might be a need for further adjustments, so please let us know if you encounter this issue.

5. Added the Bastion as a location that can be traveled to using the town portal skill.

notes.title: Restore default keys and a few other things
notes.content:
The next update will be ready in about two hours. Here's what it includes:

1. Added a button to restore default keys in the controls menu.

2. In the controls menu, mouse buttons will now be named 'RMB' (Right Mouse Button) and 'MMB' (Middle Mouse Button) instead of 'Mouse1' and 'Mouse2'.

3. The tutorial has been corrected to display 'Middle Mouse Button' for free look since it was still showing 'Right Mouse Button' as assigned to this action. This was an oversight after the default keys were changed.

4. Corrected the symbol of the healer in Cathlana, so it now displays the correct one.

5. Fixed a few typos.

Upcoming update:

1. I'm currently working on a function that shows whether all enemies have been defeated in an area and if all loot has been collected. However, this feature is not ready yet. I'm hoping to have it available by the end of the week.

2. I will also add the ability to individually adjust the volume of combat music and out-of-combat world ambiance since they are currently controlled by the same slider

notes.title: Highlighting Enemies on Mouseover and a Few Other Things
notes.content:
The next update is ready in a few hours:

1. Made enemies highlight on mouseover, to make it easier to see which enemy is targeted when enemies are standing close together.

2. Added an option in the 'Other Options' menu to disable character voices.

3. Corrected a bug that was introduced in the previous update when correcting a typo for the item 'Mana Thief' that meant that the ring lost its ability to steal mana.

4. Corrected a few more typos.

notes.title: Town portal skill for the ranger, and some minor corrections
notes.content:
The next update is ready in a short while:

1. Added a new skill to the ranger called 'Town Portal.' This skill enables the ranger to teleport the party to any village teleport that has already been discovered. The skill unlocks at level 20. If your characters have already reached that level, it will automatically be added to the skill book when you load your game.

2. Corrected a minor bug from the previous update related to the auto-walk function. If you activated auto-walk and used the run key to set auto-walk to run speed, run speed would persist when the function was disabled and would only return to normal walk speed if the run key was pressed once more. This has now been fixed.

3. Corrected some typos.

notes.title: Added stash and made some corrections
notes.content:
The next update will be ready in a couple of hours with the following changes:

1. Added a stash that can also function as an extension of the inventory, allowing you to add items to the stash no matter where you are. However, you must be at one of the stash locations to withdraw items from the stash. Adding or withdrawing items can be done by hovering the mouse over an item and using the "Move Item To Stash/Inventory Key." This action is set to "L" by default but can be changed in the controls menu. Access to the stash must be bought through one of the newly added NPCs with a chest icon. The stash can hold up to 48 items, similar to the inventory.

2. Corrected an issue where some loot objects in the maze gave no loot. This has now been fixed, but it will only work for new games or if you haven't yet been to Etyrial.

3. Fixed a bug that sometimes added duplicates of quest updates to the quest log if you first obtained the quest after completing some of the steps in the quest.

4. Added a notification that tells you when you have completed a quest step, even if you did not have the quest at the time. This change aims to address some confusion regarding why clicking on some objects sometimes seemed to do nothing.

notes.title: New skills for the warrior and the ranger
notes.content:
In a short while, the next update will be released.

1. Added a new skill to the warrior called 'Up Close And Personal.' This skill triples an enemy's move points and forces it to move towards the warrior. The skill unlocks at level 10. If your characters have already reached that level, it will automatically be added to the skill book when you load your game.

2. Added a new skill to the ranger called 'Quick Action.' This skill enables the ranger to perform an extra action in that turn. The skill unlocks at level 10. If your characters have already reached that level, it will automatically be added to the skill book when you load your game.

3. Added a sound effect to the spell 'Eye In The Sky' that plays when the spell wears off.

4. The mouse cursor didn't change to the golden in-game cursor before a game was started. This has been corrected, so the cursor is already set in the main menu when the game is booted up.

notes.title: Cursor fix and minor corrections
notes.content:
The next update is now live:

1. Since some are still reporting that the cursor sometimes shifts out of interact mode when in combat and using skills and spells, I have now added a new option in the 'Other Options' menu: 'Always Show Cursor In Combat.' Activating this option will force the cursor into interact mode as long as you are in combat, with the exception of pressing the free-look key, which will still allow you to look around without bringing the cursor to the edge of the screen.

2. After the previous update that allowed shop windows to be closed with the escape key, it was possible for the item info window to remain on the screen after the shop window was closed when using escape. This happened if the cursor was over an item when escape was pressed. This issue has now been fixed.

3. The dialogue option to decline resurrecting a character at the healers did not work. So, the only way to exit the resurrect dialogue was to select a character to resurrect, regardless of whether it was needed or not. This has now been corrected.

notes.title: Extra quick slots, inverted mouse option, and more.
notes.content:
The next update will soon be released. The update contains the following:

1. The free look function that allows you to look around in interactive mode when holding down the right mouse button has shown to be suboptimal. This caused problems like forcing you to remap the key bindings for the enemy info window because it was no longer possible to hover the mouse over a buff or debuff that was active on an enemy. Now, the function has its own key, so you can map it as you please. The default button is the middle mouse button but can be changed in the key configuration options, which you probably want to do if you already have this key mapped to something else.

2. It’s no longer possible to discard silver weapons before the quest in which they are needed has been completed.

3. You can now close the map by pressing the 'Escape' key.

4. You can now close shop windows by pressing the 'Escape' key.

5. An option to invert the mouse has been added to the other options menu.

6. A minor correction to a cliff in Micirida that was missing a collider.

7. Two extra quick slots have been added, bringing the total up to 6 quick slots.

8. On the map, there are now indications of North, South, East, and West.

9. A tree ent in Rasunda has been corrected since it was visible even though it was in ambush mode.

10. Several typos have been corrected.

notes.title: Map update, quick character selection, and some corrections
notes.content:
The next update will be ready in about two hours and will contain:

1. Added hotkeys for selecting party members. F1 to F4 will now select characters 1 to 4, but this can be modified in the controls menu.

2. The map has been revised to be horizontal rather than vertical. Additionally, the map has been better fitted to the screen, and zooming now centers on the view.

3. Some items contained typos in their effects, causing the stats not to be recognized and applied when using the item. This issue has been addressed. For items already obtained before this update that had this problem, manual corrections were made for each typo. I believe I've covered all of them, but if you notice any previously acquired items still having the issue, please let me know, and I'll address it.

4. When using the right mouse button for free look in interactive mode, the cursor will now be hidden and locked in place.

5. The Berserker's Amulet has been adjusted so that frenzy can only be activated when the character's health is below 70%, as stated in its description.

6. In Olhenvey, if you attempted to traverse the pass, an invisible wall obstructed your path. This has been rectified.

7. In the buff/debuff info window, "Battle Fatigue" was misspelled. This has been corrected.

8. The buff/debuff info window and enemy info window have been updated to match the UI look of the rest, as these were overlooked during a previous UI update.

notes.title: Minor corrections
notes.content:
The next update is almost ready for release and will include:

1. A bug was identified in which a few items in the game didn't apply one of the stats to the character when equipped. This issue has now been resolved.

2. Some of the cliffs in Micirida were missing colliders, allowing players to walk through them. This has been corrected.

3. On the character creation screen, when allocating points to various attributes like strength and constitution, there was a bug that could, under specific circumstances, allow the stat to drop below 5 when changes were rejected. This has been addressed.

4. A few typos have been corrected.

notes.title: New artwork and some minor correction
notes.content:
The next update is just about ready. This update includes:

1. New character images, increasing the total number of images to choose from by more than double.

2. New loading screen art.

3. Game tips and advice will now appear on the loading screen.

4. Correction of the 'always run' option, so the state is correctly set after loading.

5. The enemy speed option reverted to 4 when loading; this issue has also been fixed.

notes.title: Minor correction and added feature
notes.content:
Within an hour's time, the next update will be released. This update contains:

1. A correction to the enemy activation zones in Lurala. If you exit the tomb of the champion in Lurala and proceed further up to the northernmost part of Lurala, monsters are not present. This has now been fixed.

2. An 'always run' option has been added to the other options menu.Sadly, I forgot to set it up on load, so the state of the 'always run' option will revert to 'disabled' every time you load a game. Therefore, if you load a game with the 'always run' option on, you will have to disable it and then re-enable it for it to be active. This will be corrected in the next update.

3. The skills (2 skills in the first row for sorcerer, warrior, and ranger, and 1 skill for the shaman) that give bonuses on level-up but don't work retroactively now have text that clearly states this.

4. Text has been added to the info of the main attributes—strength, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, dexterity, and speed—that explains which stats they influence on level up.

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
In a couple of hours, the next update will be ready. This update will include:

1. A visual makeover of the user interface (UI). I haven't been entirely satisfied with certain aspects of the UI, especially the skill tree. Therefore, I've decided to update some of the visuals, and I personally believe that the new look is significantly improved. I hope you will feel the same way. The layout and navigation remain unchanged; only the visuals have been updated.

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
A minor update that corrects the following:

1. A fault that meant if you talk to Florian in the Ruin Village before you have obtained the quest "Dark Clouds On The Horizon," you won't be able to complete the quest. However, you can still proceed with the next quest without any problems. If you have encountered this bug, it will automatically complete the "Dark Clouds On The Horizon" quest when loading your saved game.

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
Update Information

The next update is ready to be released in about two hours. The update includes:

1. It's now possible to reset a character's stats and skills. This proved to be a very complex function to add, as there are many considerations to ensure everything resets correctly. Everything should be working correctly now, but please let me know if you experience any issues with the character reset. Currently, it's only possible to reset a character's stats at the healer in the starting village in Micirida. I'll expand this option to all healers, probably in the next update.

2. It's now possible to check if a character already knows a spell when hovering the mouse over the spell book. Additionally, if you attempt to learn a spell book that the character already knows, the spell book is no longer consumed.

3. A minor bug from the previous update has been fixed, so the skill tree does not opening when switching between the two UI options any more.

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
Update Information 

The next update will be ready in about two hours. This update includes:

1. Enemies inside the area of AoE spells and skills are now highlighted to better show who will get hit.

2. Discarding an item from the inventory will now give half of its value. This way, there is a compromise between not needing to go back too often and still getting some gold from the loot that you might not have room for.

3. An 'unstuck' function has been added to the in-game menu under the exit button. This is added because some players reported getting stuck. This way, you can always use the button to get unstuck; it only works outside of combat. I would still like to know if anyone gets stuck so I can fix the level since, of course, that’s the most ideal.

4. Corrected an issue with some items, making it possible for them to have a higher minimum damage than their maximum damage.

5. The skill tree has been adjusted so it does not cover any of the character images when using the alternative UI overlay.

6. A few typos have been corrected.

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
Update Information:

This update includes the following changes:

1. Added type icons over NPCs' heads. These icons indicate the type of NPC, such as weapon trainer, armor trainer, quest giver, and more. Icons will be enabled by default, but in the options menu, there is an option to hide them, making them appear only when the highlight key is pressed.

2. Corrected a couple of typos.

3. Made minor corrections to the level geometry in Olhenvey.

4. Fixed an issue where some enemy zones in Etyrial didn't activate when approaching from a specific location, causing the enemies to not appear. This issue has now been resolved.

5. It's now possible to see the distance to the enemy in the enemy stat info window.

6. Corrected a few enemy types, vampire bats, wyverns, and manticores, so they do not appear when in ambush mode and are not activated.

7. Quick slots that were grayed out due to cooldown when combat ended didn't change their visual state for the character that was active when combat ended before selecting another character. This issue has also been fixed.

Additionally, I'm currently working on a feature that allows for the reset of a character's skills and stats. However, this task is proving to be quite complex due to the intricacies of the leveling system, so it will take some more time before it's ready.

notes.title: Update Infromation
notes.content:
Update Information:

The next update is almost ready and will be live in about two hours. This update includes:

1. A fix for performance issues when using ultra-wide screen resolutions. The fix consists of a change in the volumetric fog, which turned out to be the main reason for low FPS when running the game with ultra-wide screen resolutions. To compensate for the changes, a new option in the graphics settings called “Smooth Volumetric Fog” is now available. This should be on by default, but do check it just in case. Visually, you should not notice any changes in the quality of the volumetric fog, but performance is significantly increased. Smooth Volumetric Fog can be turned off if you are looking for even more performance, but in most cases, this should not make any noticeable difference. The performance increase achieved by this reconfiguration is not limited to users who run the game in ultra-wide screen resolutions but is across resolutions and aspect ratios. In tests, I managed to get as much as a 60 FPS increase in the best cases.

2. The menu now always returns to the default state when being opened, instead of opening up in the menu option that was last opened.

3. The ranged attack distance of green vipers has been decreased.

4. A couple of healing spells had an issue that meant that if they were assigned to a quickslot and cast from this slot after a load, without opening the spellbook first, the heal amount would be 0. This has been corrected.

notes.title: Update Infromation
notes.content:
Update Infromation:

The next update is now up and running. This update will include the following:

1. Spells and skills assigned to a quick slot can now be cast by pressing the corresponding key. You will no longer need to click the icon to cast the skill or spell, although this option is still available.

2. When a skill is on cooldown, the icon will now be grayed out, providing a visual indication that the skill is on cooldown. This eliminates the need to hover the mouse over the skill to check if it's on cooldown.

3. Small corrections have been made to the colliders of some houses to ensure that players can't get stuck.

4. A fault in the Gobbling Cave has been corrected, which caused some enemies to be wrongly activated when standing in the dead end of the cave.

5. The tutorial has been updated to include the new features.

6. info text for the skill "Double Healing" has been corrected.

7. An auto-loot function has been added, allowing you to loot enemies within range with the press of a button (default key X, but can be changed in the controls menu, like the other keys). This function only works on enemies and cannot be used to open chests and other types of loot objects. 

8. Corrections have been made so that the cursor doesn't switch away from interact mode after a skill or spell is cast from the quick slots

notes.title: Update Information
notes.content:
Update Information:

Thank you all for your feedback; I truly appreciate it. I hope to use your insights to make “A Quest That Became Legend” the best gaming experience possible. Very soon, the new update will be uploaded to Steam.

This update addresses some of the issues that have been highlighted, as well as incorporating suggestions to enhance gameplay. Please know that I will continue to update the game and address features and fixes not included in this release.

1. Minor corrections have been made to the occlusion culling in one of the dwarf tunnels.

2. A bug that made it impossible to assign mouse buttons in the control menu has been fixed. The left mouse button is hardcoded as the attack button, so this button has been blocked and cannot be assigned to another function. If necessary, this can be changed in a future update.

3. Support for ultra-wide screen resolutions has been added, and UI elements have been adjusted accordingly. I don't have access to a screen that can support these resolutions, so testing was done by simulating them. Please inform me if there are any lingering issues or problems. The game should now auto-detect these resolutions and adjust accordingly. However, the settings can also be found in the resolution options window.

4. It's now possible to move certain UI elements by dragging them with the mouse – including the Inventory screen, Character stat screen, and Character outfit screen.

5. In interact mode/cursor mode, players can now look around by holding down the right mouse button. This means there's no longer a need to move the cursor to the edge of the screen, although that option remains available.

6. Skills and spells assigned to the quick slots will now be saved. Thus, when loading a game, characters will have the same skills and spells in the quick slots as they did when the game was saved.

7. Hit effects have been added to player character's melee and ranged attacks.
